quote: We then generate question texts to construct subquestions using a language model.

We construct a dataset to evaluate the models' ability of critical reasoning in logical reading comprehension. We crowdsource free-form rationale for main questions taken from an existing dataset and use an LLM to generate subquestion texts.

In addition to the simple accuracy over the main questions (MainQ Accuracy) and subquestions (SubQ Accuracy), we calculate the accuracy across the subquestions written for the correct and incorrect original options (Selective and Eliminative SubQ Accuracy), respectively. We also calculate the Consistency score...
we manually annotate which rationale is better in terms of necessity and specificity
We ask three workers to answer each subquestion to evaluate its human answerability.

We use Amazon Mechanical Turk. The crowdworkers who took the qualification test are based in the United States, United Kingdom, or Canada, have an approval rate of at least 98%, and have at least 1,000 approved tasks.
guideline: workers are asked to compare human-written and model-generated rationales and choose which is better
Workers answer each subquestion and indicate whether the correct answer is selected, providing a majority vote for correctness.
We provide detailed instructions with eight writing examples. Through preliminary pilot studies, we define two essential criteria for writing rationales: specificity and necessity.
